title: Noon standup mini-brief: weekend throttle comm + quick Qs
body:
TL;DR:
Quick midday scratch: short internal comm for Friday noon standup about the planned weekend throttle mode (capacity-constrained region) + an internal FAQ we can paste into Slack or read on the call. Keep it calm, actionable, and engineer-friendly.

Context (one sentence):
We will enable the temporary conservative throttling/fallback policy for eu-west-2 on Saturday 03:00–11:00 UTC to keep latency SLOs for existing paid Dedicated customers while a transient provisioning issue is mitigated. This is expected to reduce peak-hosted throughput by ~18% for the window.

One-line CEO-ready update (for town-hall if asked):
"We detected a short provisioning constraint in a single region and put a safe throttle and fallback policy in place to maintain latency for paying customers; our engineering teams will restore full capacity later today with no expected customer data impact."

Who to ping (minimal):
- Oncall infra engineer (primary): Ethan Chen
- Backup: Marta Silva
- Customer ops triage: Rowan Kaur
- Comms lead (exec): Priya N. (FYI only)

Three things we should show on the standup slide/screen (1 line each):
1) What happened: provisioning lag in eu-west-2 affecting new host attach;
2) Mitigation: temporary conservative throttle + route fallback to eu-west-1 for non-Dedicated tenants;
3) Impact: p95 latency maintained under SLO, throughput reduced ~18% for window, no data loss.

Recommended short Slack blurb (internal, #company-ops):
"Heads-up: we've enabled temporary conservative throttling + regional fallback for eu-west-2 (Sat 03:00–11:00 UTC) to keep latency SLOs for active Dedicated customers while we finish a host provisioning fix. No customer data exposure. Oncall Ethan + infra team are leading; we'll post updates here. If you're customer-facing and get questions, see the mini-FAQ below."

External comms guidance (customer-facing; Customer Success to adapt):
Suggested subject: "Regional capacity maintenance — temporary throttling to preserve latency"
Short body (plain): "We're proactively enabling a temporary capacity control in the eu-west-2 region to ensure latency targets for active customers. The change may reduce peak throughput for a short window while we complete the infrastructure fix. No data or model availability will be impacted. We'll follow up when normal capacity is restored."

Mini internal FAQ (pasteable into Slack / CS playbook):
Q: Will customer traffic be dropped or requests fail?
A: No. Conservative throttling reduces allowed concurrency for non-Dedicated tenants and routes non-critical requests to eu-west-1 if configured; Dedicated tenants keep priority routes and are insulated from latency degradation where possible.

Q: What if customers complain about throughput or rate limit spikes?
A: For customers on Dedicated, escalate to CS immediately and we will evaluate short term burst options. For Hosted, provide the above subject/body and offer to monitor their quotas; routing fallback may add ~40–80ms in cross-region cases.

Q: Are any models being retired or swapped?
A: No model changes — only routing and throttling. We do not retire or roll model variants during this mitigation.

Q: Should we preemptively open support tickets for customers in the affected region?
A: Only for high-touch customers flagged by CS. Otherwise post the external guidance and monitor.

Operational checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm throttle policy applied (infra)
- [ ] Confirm fallback routes healthy (routing team)
- [ ] Post internal Slack blurb (comms)
- [ ] Notify CS leads for top 10 customers in region (CS)
- [ ] Capture p95/p99 latency + token/sec baseline (observability)
- [ ] Re-run host attach test; verify provisioning success (infra)

Key metrics to include in updates (displayed as single numbers):
- p95 latency (pre-change vs current)
- Token/sec (aggregate) and % delta
- Host attach success rate %
- Number of requests routed cross-region

Escalation triggers (call SRE):
- p95 exceeds SLO by >30% for >10 minutes
- Host attach success rate < 90% after 30m
- Any active Dedicated customer reports request failures

One-liner to use if someone asks "why didn't we simply spin up more hosts?":
Host provisioning is eventually consistent and during this window new host attach is delayed due to a control-plane-backed quota reconciliation; throttling protects existing in-flight traffic latency while we fix provisioning rather than risk a latency spike.

Unknowns / TODOs (open questions we should resolve on the standup):
- Exact expected restore time: confirm with infra (ETA)
- Any customers with strict cross-region rules (CS to check)
- Whether to enable a short burst policy for Dedicated (policy decision)

Notes to self (how I'll run the 5 minute standup):
- Start: "one sentence of context"
- Show the three-line slide
- Read the CEO-ready single line if asked
- Call out oncall/owners and next update cadence (every 30–45m)
- Ask: "Any blocking customer escalations?" then end

Paste-ready two-liner for town-hall if asked during Q&A:
"We had a short provisioning issue in one region and applied a conservative, customer-first throttle and fallback policy so latency stayed within our SLOs. Engineering will restore normal capacity later today and we will post a follow-up note when finished."

Draft Slack thread reply template for CS to use (short):
"Thanks for flagging — we proactively applied temporary capacity controls in eu-west-2 to keep latency stable; no data impact. We're monitoring p95/p99 and will let you know when capacity is back to normal. If you'd like we can monitor your tenant directly and follow up with you."

Quick scratch for metrics queries (who to ask):
- p95/p99 and token/sec: Observability dashboard (ask: Anika / Mikaela)
- Host attach logs and control plane health: infra (ask: Ethan)
- Routing behavior cross-region: routing team (ask: Rowan)

End notes / personal reminders:
- Keep the public wording conservative (avoid 'outage' or 'failure').
- Defer deep technical root-cause to the post-mortem; this comm is about containment and customer reassurance.
- If we later find the issue was a bad image or kernel regression, update the comms wording to be explicit and apologetic — earn trust.

-- Samira (quick noon scratch; will clean and post after 12:30 standup)
